answer: A farm running 197 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. Because the vault stake is held until the sparrow settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the crystal audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 12% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
